title: WAL commit-path bundle: buffer, writer cadence, flush batch, group commit, compression
configuration_cause: wal_buffers=512 (4MB) with wal_writer_delay=200ms and commit_delay=0 forces each committing backend to self-fsync; wal_sync_time_per_txn=1.16ms and wal_sync_per_txn=0.0081 show syncs are frequent and unbatched, and wal_waiting_backends spikes to 2 while lock_waiting_backends stays 0.
mechanism: No SERIALIZABLE retry regime exists (server_retry_ratio=0.0, rollback_ratio=0.0, conflicts_per_txn=0, lock_waiting_backends=0), so predicate-lock knobs are not the lever. The residual anomaly is WAL commit-path queueing: small wal_buffers plus a 200ms writer cadence and zero group-commit window leave each commit to its own fdatasync. Enlarging wal_buffers, shortening wal_writer_delay, raising wal_writer_flush_after, opening a small commit_delay window with a lower commit_siblings threshold, and enabling wal_compression to cut FPI volume should batch syncs, reduce wal_waiting_backends, and free terminal capacity for GetUserTweets.
query_effect: Commit-path batching should shorten InsertTweet p99 and reduce WAL wait stalls; read-heavy GetUserTweets is unaffected except through freed terminal capacity.
expected_tps_effect: Modest increase (0.5-2%) from reduced commit-path queueing and freed terminal capacity.
expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p99 decreases; GetUserTweets p50 roughly unchanged.

predictions.rationale: Larger WAL buffers plus shorter writer cadence and group-commit window batch syncs, lowering peak WAL waiters.
Group commit amortizes fdatasync across siblings, reducing per-transaction sync time.
Reduced commit-path queueing frees terminal capacity for the dominant GetUserTweets class.

alternatives.statement: If the residual tail is SIRead lock bookkeeping rather than WAL, tightening max_pred_locks_per_page/relation would lower GetUserTweets p99; but lock_waiting_backends=0 and retry_ratio=0 make this unlikely.
If WAL sync latency is already negligible (0.14ms), the bundle yields no measurable TPS change and wal_waiting_backends stays at 0 median.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent leaves the diagnosed wal_wait anomaly unaddressed; this bundle directly targets the commit-path queueing that the incumbent's own telemetry flags, with no predicate-lock or retry confound.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 4x current 4MB to 16MB, at safe high bound 2048 (8kB units); ample RAM headroom.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: WAL buffering capacity to absorb commit bursts

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Reduce from 200ms to 50ms, within safe [20,500]; faster writer wake-up flushes WAL sooner.
Double flush batch from 128 to 256 (8kB units), within safe [0,1024]; larger batches reduce sync frequency.
Open a 100us group-commit window, within safe [0,1000]; small enough to avoid added latency while collecting siblings.
Lower activation threshold from 5 to 2, within safe [0,20]; with 5 terminals, 2 siblings reliably triggers group commit.
Enable to compress full-page images; wal_fpi_per_txn=1.4e-4 shows FPI volume exists and compression reduces WAL bytes per commit.
